chapter_theme: The supreme states (பராவத்தை): the soul's states of waking, dream, deep sleep and turiya are traced up through grades to Siva's own turiya, where, beyond the thirty-six tattvas and by grace, the bonds fall away and the soul becomes one with Siva. Images of gold and ornament, wood and elephant show how the Supreme and the world each hide the other.
structure_note: The Lord beyond the five and the thirty-six (2269 to 2271); the grades of turiya, from the soul's to Siva's, with the union they lead to (2272 to 2285); the Lord's descending order (2286); self-knowledge and mutual concealment (2287 to 2290); the five-letter mantra and the pure supreme state in which the malas end (2291 to 2295).

2269.reading: I came to know how the beginningless supreme God beyond the five, the stainless unborn one who became the heart, stayed hidden so as to set the body and the soul apart.
2269.nuance: அஞ்சும் கடந்த (beyond the five) is not explained: the five senses, the five states or the five malas are all possible. வஞ்சத்து இருந்த (stayed in concealment) suggests the Lord's hiding act, but the verse doesn't name it.

2270.reading: The verse lists Shakti in her grades, as Paraparai, in peace (சாந்தி), in supreme bliss, as radiant bindu, as true maya and with the body's five powers, and the soul that receives Shakti makes the sixth in the limbs.
2270.nuance: The line divisions and the count (ஐந்துடன், ஆறுமே) are obscure; சாந்தி may be one of the kalas and சத்திய மாயை is perhaps pure maya. Only the general sense, Shakti descending in grades to the embodied soul, is secure.

2271.reading: Those who know are beyond the thirty-six; those who receive grace are beyond it; for them knowledge is beyond it, and beyond it Hara is sweet.
2271.nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the usual way of naming the thirty-six tattvas. The refrain makes the point by repetition: knowing, grace and the sweetness of Siva all lie past the constituents of body and world.

2272.reading: Passing the five and the four and entering within, the king of the vidyadharas, asleep on his soft bed, seeks out the gentle woman with longing and takes his pleasure.
2272.nuance: A plain erotic image with a symbolic sense: the five and the four are usually taken as the five senses and the four inner instruments, the sleeping king as the soul in the yogic sleep of turiya, and the woman as Shakti. நஞ்சுற (so that poison enters) is hard to fit; it may be a corruption, perhaps of நெஞ்சுற (with the heart).

2273.reading: In the waking proper to turiya she (Shakti) is present; across waking and the two after it lies the rare turiya; in the vast para-turiya is the Supreme; and in the turiya reached by turning back, Siva.
2273.nuance: நனாத்துரியம், பரதுரியம் and the turiya reached by turning (திரிய) are technical grades of the states, assigned here to Shakti, the Supreme and Siva. How the second line fits the scheme is unclear.

2274.reading: The Supreme, the state beyond (அதீதம்), is grasped as attachment ends and becomes one's own as one practises it again and again; ascetics who don't practise it don't become the Supreme, since not one of their bonds and attachments ends.
2274.nuance: பற்றறப் பற்ற plays on பற்று: one grasps the Supreme by letting go of grasping. The verse is aimed at ascetics (தபோதனர்) whose austerity lacks this practice.

2275.reading: False maya, which one examines, stands inside and outside; if one passes beyond breath and mind and that confusion ends, pure knowledge becomes the bliss of Siva and itself grows into the reality that covers all.
2275.nuance: வேயும் பொருள் (the thing that covers or roofs) is obscure; it may mean the reality that pervades everything. வாயு is the breath, stilled with the mind in yoga.

2276.reading: The Lord set the soul that rode the horse of turiya inside the great tiger and drove the jackals running, and the deeds bound to that soul stood there and wailed.
2276.nuance: Wholly symbolic: the jackals are usually taken as the senses or the malas, the tiger as Siva or his grace, and the wailing deeds as karma left without a hold. The verse does not name any of these.

2277.reading: In this waking that stands in long turiya, the Lord of the hall stands ready to marry; when he marries, maya vanishes, and that day this soul takes his form.
2277.nuance: மன்றன் is Siva of the hall (அம்பலம்) where he dances. Marriage stands for the soul's union with him, and அவன்வடிவாமே for the soul taking Siva's form. சாக்கிர நீள்துரியம் is a technical state.

2278.reading: When waking spreads out it becomes like a lamp; where it stays, maya stands to match it; the turiya one enters becomes one's own working, and in the turiya one comes to know, evil does not remain.
2278.nuance: The last words தீதுஅகலாதே can mean 'evil does not leave' as easily as 'evil leaves without fail', and the two give opposite senses; the context of the chapter favours the second, but the text does not decide it. ஈடான and புரியல்தானாகும் are also obscure.

2279.reading: Not knowing you, I once took myself to be one with the body; knowing you, you stood with me in turiya; and since birth does not end merely by knowing oneself, know that the one who pervades is the Stainless.
2279.nuance: The verse separates knowing oneself, which does not end rebirth, from knowing the pervading Lord (வியாத்தன்). The shifts of person (I, you, oneself) make the speaker and addressee hard to fix.

2280.reading: While the body, bounded by the womb, and turiya are two, the two pass through birth and death; once those who have the guru's boon unite, there are no longer two, and they stand as one.
2280.nuance: இருவரும் (the two) is read here as the body and turiya, but it can also be the soul and the Lord, which makes the last line a statement of union. Either way the guru's grace (குருவரம்) is what ends the duality.

2281.reading: In the soul's turiya there is waking, in the soul's stirring there is dream, in its stillness the para-atita as deep sleep, and in service para-turiya is the Supreme.
2281.nuance: அணு is the soul as atom-like, the bound soul. The verse maps the ordinary states onto higher ones, and பணியில் (in service, or in humility) is obscure.

2282.reading: In para-turiya there is a waking that spreads, a dream that has swallowed the wide world, a true peace and a deep sleep that takes form; as these cease, one is seen to be in Siva's turiya.
2282.nuance: The verse sets out the four states again at the higher level of para-turiya. Each name (சாந்தி, சுழுத்தி) is technical, and the exact grades are the tradition's.

2283.reading: After the supreme waking come the steady dream that has eaten the world, the excellent deep sleep and the strong upasanta calm; to reach these is renunciation, and one becomes the bearer of Siva's turiya.
2283.nuance: A near-variant of 2282. உபசாந்தம் is a technical name for a state of calm; துறவே may mean renunciation itself or 'by renouncing'.

2284.reading: From the soul's turiya up to Siva's turiya-end, the ten states cease in their order; dwelling in the truth of supreme Nandi, he stood having freed the soul from the twenty-eight.
2284.nuance: அவத்தைபத்தும் (the ten states) and நாலேழ் (four sevens, twenty-eight, or four and seven) are counts from the tradition's scheme that the verse doesn't spell out.

2285.reading: Above Paramasiva is the Paramam; in that Para, Paramasiva above becomes the supreme waking; the sushumna that ends the distress of the spreading dream gives strength: this is the truth of great Nandi.
2285.nuance: கழுமுனை is the sushumna, the central channel of yoga. The ordering of Paramasiva and Paramam is the tradition's and the syntax of the verse is loose.

2286.reading: When seen, the order runs: Paramasiva who is the support, Shakti, supreme nada, bindu above it and Sadasiva rising high, then below them Brahma, Hari, the god of the immortals' city, Rudra and Isa.
2286.nuance: A list of Siva's descending forms in Siddhanta. பாலாய் may mean 'below' or 'as milk'; அமராபதி தேவாம் (the god of Amaravati) would usually be Indra, an odd entry here, so it may describe one of the others.

2287.reading: Those who don't know the union, nor the end of the seven sea-girt worlds, nor how the soul stands with the body, and cannot rule here having understood the turmoil, aim only at outward show and force.
2287.nuance: கலப்பு (mingling) may be the soul's union with Siva or the mixing of soul and body. அலப்பு, அரசாளகிலாதார் and the last line (குறிப்பது கோலம் அடலது வாமே) are obscure; this reading is a guess.

2288.reading: If one knows oneself through the truth of great austerity that is known afterwards, the compassionate Supreme is our Lord; and when former knowledge comes to its end, I set out to know myself and so came to joy.
2288.nuance: The traditional saying that one who knows oneself knows the Lord fits this verse, but the first line is hard to construe. முன்னை அறிவு (former knowledge) may be the bound soul's ordinary knowing.

2289.reading: The gold ornament hides the gold, and the gold ornament disappears into the gold; one's own instruments hide oneself, and one's instruments disappear into oneself.
2289.nuance: Seen as an ornament, the gold is not noticed; seen as gold, the ornament is not. So too the soul and its faculties (கரணங்கள்): attention to one hides the other. தன் is usually taken as the soul.

2290.reading: The great rutting elephant hides the wood, and the elephant disappears into the wood; the elements beginning with earth hide the Supreme, and the elements disappear into the Supreme.
2290.nuance: The image is a wooden elephant: one who sees the elephant doesn't see the wood, and one who sees the wood doesn't see the elephant. Seeing the world hides the Lord in it; seeing the Lord, the world vanishes into him.

2291.reading: Passing beyond the thirty-six and leaving 'na-ma', the soul becomes knowledge and, standing apart, rises as 'ya'; reaching the Tatpara free of darkness beyond Para, release follows, gathered in 'Si-va-ya'.
2291.nuance: The verse reads the five-letter mantra (நமசிவாய) as a path: dropping நம, traditionally the syllables of the bonds, leaves சிவாய, in which ய is the soul. The letter symbolism is the tradition's and the syntax is compressed.

2292.reading: In turiya the five are the letters beginning with A; in Para spreading out, nada and its end prevail; in Para there is the awareness of the supreme state, and as it turns, the supreme turiya becomes clear.
2292.nuance: அகராதி (the letters from A) may be the five letters of the mantra or the parts of Om. பராவத்தா போதம் names the chapter's subject, but the verse gives no clear account of it.

2293.reading: By grace the five states in the sakala condition cease to work; in the stirring of the pure state, as one seeks Nandi's supreme state, the five malas leave like evening darkness before a flame.
2293.nuance: சகலம் (the embodied condition) and சுத்தம் (the pure) are two of the soul's three conditions in Siddhanta. ஐம்மலம் counts five malas, where the tradition often counts three. The darkness-and-light simile is plain.

2294.reading: When the purusha sees through the twenty-five, measured prakriti, maya and the great maya seen to be false, and becomes all of them and none of them, the saving supreme state is reached: to contemplate it is purity.
2294.nuance: ஐஐந்து (five fives) is taken as the twenty-five lower tattvas. எய்யும் படியாய் (so as to shoot through, or to attain) is obscure.

2295.reading: The Lord of nada in good knowledge is the one in whom his grace, the Supreme and the love that came first become one, in whom form and limiting adjunct merge, and who left me and went there yet did not go.
2295.nuance: உபாதி (limiting adjunct) is a technical term. The paradox of going and not going (சென்றான், செல்லாமை) may be the Lord's transcendence and immanence; the verse's construction is loose.

links.note: Paired images of mutual concealment: gold and ornament for the soul and its faculties, wood and carved elephant for the Lord and the elements.
2288 makes knowing oneself the way to know the Lord; 2279 adds that knowing oneself alone doesn't end birth unless one knows the pervading Lord.
Both play on பற்று: the Kural bids one cling to the one without clinging in order to let go, Tirumular says the Supreme is grasped as attachment ends.

2269 says the beginningless Lord stayed in concealment (வஞ்சத்து இருந்த) so as to set body and soul apart; 111 says he stands hidden (கரத்தினுள் நின்று) and works dissolution (கழிவுசெய்தானே). Both make the parting of body and soul, or the world's dissolution, the work of a Lord who acts while unseen.

2275 says that when maya's confusion ends past breath and mind, pure knowledge itself becomes Siva's bliss (தூய அறிவு சிவானந்தமாகி); 1587 says Siva-knowledge gives Siva's bliss (சிவமான ஞானம் சிவானந்தம் நல்குமே). The two make knowledge, not practice alone, the thing that turns into bliss.

In 121 வியாக்கிரத்தே, read as 'in waking', is where pure turiya arises; in 2276 the soul on turiya's horse is put inside the great வியாக்கிரம், read as 'tiger'. The pairing suggests 2276's tiger may also be a play on waking, which fits the chapter's teaching that turiya is reached within waking.

2277 says that when the Lord of the hall marries the soul, maya vanishes and the soul becomes his form (அவன்வடிவாமே); 2013 says souls who practised of old will later see and take Siva's form within (சிவனுருக் கொள்வர்). Both name the end as the soul taking Siva's form, 2277 through union and 2013 through long practice.

2279 says birth does not end even when one knows oneself (தன்னை அறிந்தும் பிறவி தணவாதால்), so one must know the pervading Stainless One; 2331 says birth ends (பிறப்பறும்) when one knows oneself and becomes oneself with Siva (சிவனுடன் தானாக). 2331 supplies the condition 2279 says self-knowledge lacks: union with Siva.

2280 says that once those who have the guru's boon (குருவரம்) unite, the two are gone and they stand as one; 1608 says Nandi changed the thirty-six in him and made him Siva (சிவமாக்கி). Both make the guru the one who ends the division between soul and Lord.

Both verses use the same scheme and words: the soul's turiya (அணுவின் துரியம்) holding the lower states, and a para-turiya tied to பணி (பணியில் பரதுரியம் in 2281, பணியும் பரதுரியம் in 2468). 2468, in a distant chapter, is a near-restatement of 2281 that adds how the two sets of four combine into five.

2282 sets waking, a dream that swallows the world, peace and deep sleep inside para-turiya, ending in Siva's turiya; 2444 says that in para-turiya waking is absorbed (பரதுரியத்து நனவு படியுண்ட), dream spreads, and calm (உபசாந்தம்) leads to the rare turiya at Siva. 2444, in a distant chapter, is a near-repeat of the scheme in 2282 and 2283.

2282 maps the states within para-turiya (பரதுரியத்து) on the way to Siva's turiya. Thiruppugazh 203 asks for the light beyond the thirty-six and beyond para-turiya (பரதுரி யாதீதம்), which it says no master of yoga reaches. Arunagiri uses the Tirumanthiram's technical grade பரதுரியம் and places the goal past it.

2283 is a near-variant of 2282: both run waking, a dream that has eaten the world (சகமுண்ட / சகம் உண்ட கனவு), deep sleep and calm up to Siva's turiya (சிவதுரியத்தனும் ஆமே). 2283 adds that reaching these is renunciation (துறவே).

2284 says Nandi stood having freed the soul from the நாலேழ் (twenty-eight) after the ten states cease; 2176 counts the twenty-eight tattvas (தத்துவ நாலேழ்), including turiya and the higher turiya. Read with 2176, 2284's obscure count may be these tattvas, from which the soul is released.

2285 says the sushumna (கழுமுனை) ends the distress of the spreading dream within the supreme waking of Para; 2444 places the sushumna (துரிய கழுமுனை) in the calm of para-turiya, before cessation at Siva. Both put the yogic channel inside the higher states, not only in breath practice.

2286 lists Siva's descending forms: Paramasiva, Shakti, supreme nada, bindu and Sadasiva, then Brahma, Hari, Rudra and Isa; 384 gives the same order of emergence, light becoming Shakti, nada becoming bindu, and Sadasiva as support of the five elements. 384 shows the sequence in 2286 is a creation sequence.

2288 says that if one knows oneself (தன்னை அறியில்) the compassionate Supreme is our Lord, and the speaker came to joy by setting out to know himself; 2349 says the one who knows himself within himself goes on to know his Lord within himself (தன் ஐ அறியத் தலைப்படும்). Both make self-knowledge the way to knowing the Lord.

Both use gold and its ornaments. 1087 says the many gods are like the many ornaments (பூணும் பலபல பொன்போல) that are all gold, to show one Mistress as cause; 2289 says the ornament hides the gold (பொன்னை மறைத்தது பொன்னணி பூடணம்), to show how the faculties hide the soul. The same image teaches unity in 1087 and concealment in 2289.

2291 reads the mantra as a path: dropping நம, the soul rises as ய and release comes in சிவாய; 979 says சிவாய, joined, becomes the soul, enjoyment and knowledge, and becoming Siva by it is release (அச்சிவம் ஆவது வீடே). 2291 spells out the letter-by-letter path to the release that 979 names.

2293 says the five malas leave like evening darkness before a flame (சுடர்முனம் அந்தி இருள்போலும் ஐம்மலம் மாறுமே); Naladiyar 51 says sin cannot stand before austerity, as darkness dies when a lamp enters (விளக்குப் புக இருள் மாய்ந்தாங்கு). The same image does the work of grace in one verse and of tapas in the other, and the Naladiyar adds that darkness returns when the oil runs out.

1517 says Nandi, wrapped in grace, comes into the confusion of delusion like a lamp brought into a dark room (இருள்சூழ் அறையில்... விளக்கு); 2293 says that by grace (அருளால்) the malas leave like darkness before a flame. Both verses use the image of light and darkness for grace.

2295 says the Lord of nada left me and went there yet did not go (சென்றான்... செல்லாமையும்); 1628 says he is hidden yet not hidden (கரந்துங் கரந்திலன்). Both describe the Lord's presence as a paradox of being both gone and present.

source_issues: 2290: line 4 reads பரத்தை மறைந்தது, where the pattern of line 2 and of 2289 needs பரத்தின் (or பரத்தில்) மறைந்தது.
2272: நஞ்சுற (so that poison enters) fits the image poorly and may be corrupt, perhaps for நெஞ்சுற.
